description_full: PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk, together with its subsidiaries, provides telecommunication, telecommunications network, and multimedia services for consumers and businesses in Indonesia. It operates through the GSM Mobile and Telecommunications Network Services, and Managed and Information Technology Services. The company provides cellular mobile and closed fixed network, Internet, Internet telephony and interconnection, data communication system, packet switched local fixed network, telephony, and voice over Internet protocol services. It also offers digital content and home broadband services; voice and short message services; data and digital services; mobile communication services; call center services; and other telecommunication services, such as subscriber identity module (SIM) cards, and leased lines and towers. PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk was formerly known as PT XL Axiata Tbk and changed its name to PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tbk in April 2025. The company was founded in 1989 and is headquartered in Jakarta Selatan, Indonesia.

financial_summary: PT XLSMART Telecom Sejahtera Tb is a small-cap communication services business with a $1.5B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size. Operating margins are contracting by -4.4pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 5% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests. Gross margins of 63% confirm genuine pricing power.
The business throws off $455M in free cash flow — roughly 19 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, thin -0.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 13.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.0× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
